claim.quote: Here we report the detection of Very High Energy (VHE) gamma-ray emission from Crab Nebula above 80 GeV.

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date; journal reference as printed on the arXiv page: Astroparticle Physics 159 (2024) 102960.

key_value_text.quote: The gamma-rays are detected in an energy range spanning from 80 GeV to ~5 TeV.
key_value_text.value: Crab detected from 80 GeV to about 5 TeV

name: MACE detects the Crab Nebula above 80 GeV
notes: No significance is recorded: the abstract states none.

summary.plain: The 21 metre MACE telescope in the Indian Himalayas detected gamma rays from the Crab Nebula above 80 GeV in about 15 hours of data, in a first-light analysis of observations from November 2022 to February 2023.
summary.technical: About 15 hours of low-zenith-angle data (November 2022 - February 2023): log-parabola spectrum with flux (3.46 +- 0.26 stat) x 10^-10 TeV^-1 cm^-2 s^-1 at 400 GeV, index 2.09 +- 0.06 stat; detection from 80 GeV to about 5 TeV; energy resolution about 34% at 80 GeV improving to about 21% above 1 TeV.

title: Observations of the Crab Nebula with MACE (Major Atmospheric Cherenkov Experiment)
why_it_matters: The paper presents the first-light results from the Crab Nebula for the newly commissioned telescope and notes that it is the only operational imaging Cherenkov telescope at such a high altitude.
